newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA'S VILNIAUS BANK SAYS ASSETS UP 2.4 TIMES.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA'S VILNIAUS BANK SAYS ASSETS UP 2.4 TIMES.

text.p: Lithuania's leading private bank, Vilniaus Bank, said on Monday that its assets grew by 2.4 times in 1996.
"In 1996, total assets more than doubled, from LTL 382.9 million up to LTL 914.7 million, an increase of 139 percent," the bank said in a statement.
"Profit generated over the period and the successfully placed new share issue pushed the shareholders' equity up to LTL 117.1 million, an increase of 3.7 times," the bank added.
Vilniaus Bank last year became the first company in the former Soviet Union to issue a global depository receipts (GDR) issue. The issue was worth $17.1 million and was oversubscribed.
The bank last year also boosted its share capital from 42 million litas to 102 million litas.
Analysts say the bank has benefited from a crisis which rocked the sector in late 1995, picking up business and customers from other Lithuanian banks, many of them troubled.
